html:
A series of floods on the Yangtze, Huai and other rivers of central China from June to August 1931. They are counted among the deadliest natural disasters ever recorded, though the death toll is much disputed.

Heavy snowmelt and then unusually heavy rains swelled the rivers. Dikes failed along hundreds of kilometres. Wuhan was under water for weeks, the waters reached the capital Nanjing, and in August a dike broke on Lake Gaoyou, drowning many people in their sleep.

A survey at the time by the University of Nanking found that about 150,000 people drowned, and that this was well under a quarter of the deaths in the first hundred days. Many more died of hunger and disease such as cholera. Official figures put the dead at about two million; some later estimates are higher still.

The Nationalist government set up a relief commission. Weeks later Japan seized Manchuria, and the government's attention turned to war. The Yangtze floods led in time to giant control works such as the Three Gorges Dam.
sum: A series of floods on the Yangtze, Huai and other rivers of central China from June to August 1931. They are counted among the deadliest natural disasters ever recorded, though the death toll is much disputed.
